## 1. Primary Endpoint (with timepoint)
- **Endpoint:** Change from Baseline in HbA1c (%)
- **Timepoint:** Week 24
- **Analysis population:** ITT (primary efficacy analysis set)

## 2. Secondary Endpoints
| # | Endpoint | Timepoint | Type |
|---|----------|-----------|------|
| 1 | HbA1c < 7.0% (responder / target threshold) | Week 24 | Binary (responder) |
| 2 | Body weight change | *(not explicitly specified in excerpt)* | Continuous |

## 3. Population Definitions (exact criteria from SAP)
| Population | Inclusion Criteria |
|------------|-------------------|
| **ITT (Intent-to-Treat)** | All randomized subjects who received at least one dose of study treatment (randomized + dosed) |
| **Safety** | All subjects who received any dose of study treatment (any exposure) |
| **PP (Per-Protocol)** | Subjects with no major protocol deviations affecting the primary endpoint |

> **Note:** The ITT definition here combines randomization with treatment exposure ("randomized + dose"). This is technically an **mITT / modified ITT** convention. A strict **ITT** would include all randomized subjects regardless of dosing. Flag this terminology with the sponsor/biostatistician — if regulatory review expects a true ITT (all randomized), the SAP label may need clarification or a separate "true ITT" set defined.

## 4. Statistical Method
- **Primary analysis:** **MMRM** (Mixed Model for Repeated Measures)
- **Applies to:** Primary endpoint (Change from Baseline in HbA1c at Week 24)
- **Implied model structure** (standard MMRM conventions to confirm in SAP): treatment group, baseline HbA1c as covariate, visit (Week × treatment interaction), unstructured covariance for repeated within-subject measures, REML estimation.

## Machine-Readable Shell (YAML)

Per the output schema in `tfl-table-generator`, the structured definition:

```yaml
table_output:
  table_id: "Table 14.1.3"
  title: "Demographics by Treatment Group (Safety Analysis Set)"
  population: "SAFFL"

  format: "rtf"
```

## Formatting Standards Applied

| Element | Specification |

| Orientation | Landscape (multi-column table) |

| Title font | Courier New, 10pt, Bold |

| Page numbering | "Page X of Y" (bottom center) |
| Header (top) | `Protocol: {study_id}` ... `Confidential` |

---

## Computation Logic (per `tfl-table-generator`)

**Continuous (AGE):**
- **n** = count of non-missing AGE within each TRT01P group
- **Mean (SD)** = `f"{mean:.1f} ({std(ddof=1):.2f})"`
- **Median** = `f"{median:.1f}"`
- **Min, Max** = `f"{min:.0f}, {max:.0f}"`

**Categorical (SEX, RACE):**
- **n** = count per category within each TRT01P group
- **%** = `(n / N_group) * 100`, formatted to 1 decimal → `f"{n} ({pct:.1f})"`
- **Total column** = pooled across all arms, recomputed independently

- ✅ All three arms present with **dynamically computed** column N values (no hardcoded N)

- ✅ Zero/empty categories shown as `0 (0.0%)`, not suppressed

- ✅ Matches approved shell structure — no deviation from SAP specification

## 4. Key Design Notes

- **Class assignment:** `DM` = SPECIAL PURPOSE; `AE` = EVENTS (per SDTMIG v3.4).
- **Origins:** `USUBJID`, sequence numbers, study-day variables → Derived/Assigned; `DOMAIN` → Assigned; all CRF-collected fields → CRF. This traceability matches what the aCRF finalizer skill verifies.
- **MedDRA references** (`AEDECOD`, `AEBODSYS`) use `<ExternalCodeList>` with `def:ExtendedValue="Yes"` because the full value set is dictionary-supplied, not enumerated. Update the `Version` (currently `26.1`) to match your study's locked MedDRA version.
- **COUNTRY** marked `def:ExtendedValue="Yes"` since the full ISO 3166-1 code set is large; enumerating the subset used by the study is acceptable but should be reviewed against actual `DM.COUNTRY` values.
- **Date variables** use ISO 8601 (`--DTC`), DataType `text`, Length 20 to accommodate partial dates (e.g., `2026-07` or `2026`).
- **Consistency hooks:** The variables annotated here should align exactly with `/define-draft-builder` output, the annotated CRF (verified by `/acrf-finalizer`), and the SDTM XPT datasets. Any mismatch will surface in `/adam-traceability-checker` or P21 validation.

# Demographics Table Shell

## Table Specification

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Table No.** | 14.1.1 |
| **Title** | Demographic and Baseline Characteristics by Treatment Group |
| **Analysis Set** | Safety Analysis Set (SAFFL = 'Y') — or per SAP (ITT/ITTFL) |
| **Source Dataset** | ADSL (variables: `TRT01P`, `AGE`, `SEX`, `RACE`) |
| **Treatment Variable** | `TRT01P` (Planned Treatment) |
| **Format Reference** | CDISC ADaM IG + SAP Table Shell |

---

## Table Shell (Column Layout)

```
                                               | Treatment Group
                                               | Placebo | Drug 100mg | Drug 200mg | Total
-----------------------------------------------+--------+------------+------------+------
Characteristic                                 |
-----------------------------------------------+--------+------------+------------+------
Age (years)
  n                                             |  nnn   |   nnn      |   nnn      | nnn
  Mean (SD)                                     | nn.n   |   nn.n     |   nn.n     | nn.n
                                               | (nn.n) |   (nn.n)   |   (nn.n)   | (nn.n)
  Median                                        | nn.n   |   nn.n     |   nn.n     | nn.n
  Min, Max                                      | nnn, nnn | nnn, nnn | nnn, nnn   | nnn, nnn

Sex, n (%)
  Male                                          | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n)
  Female                                        | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n)

Race, n (%)
  White                                         | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n)
  Black or African American                     | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n)
  Asian                                         | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n)
  American Indian or Alaska Native              | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n)
  Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander     | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n)
  Other                                         | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n)
  Missing / Not Reported                        | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n) | nnn (nn.n)
```

**Legend:** `nnn` = integer count; `nn.n` = 1-decimal value. Parentheses indicate the qualifier statistic paired with the preceding count.

---

## Derivation & Programming Notes (per ADSL conventions)

| Section | Statistic | Derivation from ADSL |
|---------|-----------|----------------------|
| **Age** | `n` | Count of non-missing `AGE` within `TRT01P` |
| | Mean (SD) | `MEAN(AGE)`, `STD(AGE)` — denominator = non-missing `AGE` |
| | Median | `MEDIAN(AGE)` |
| | Min, Max | `MIN(AGE), MAX(AGE)` |
| **Sex** | n (%) | Count by `SEX` level ÷ column `N` × 100. Denominator = subjects in arm (incl. missing `SEX` excluded from categories but counted in denominator) |
| **Race** | n (%) | Count by `RACE` level ÷ column `N` × 100. Denominator = column `N` |

---

## Critical Formatting Rules (FDA TFL Standards)

1. **Denominator consistency** — `n` for categorical rows uses the **column total `N`** (subjects in treatment arm), not the count with non-missing category. Percentages sum to ≤ 100% when missing exists.
2. **Decimal alignment** — Mean/SD/Median use **1 decimal**; percentages use **1 decimal** with no trailing zero suppression (e.g., `0.0`).
3. **Zero suppression** — Do **not** print rows with `n = 0` unless the SAP requires explicit "0" display. Most FDA tables suppress empty categories.
4. **Race category order** — Follow **CDISC controlled terminology (NCI CT)** order, not frequency order; or match SAP-specified order.
5. **Missing data handling** — Missing `RACE`/`SEX` values: report as separate "Missing / Not Reported" row OR footnote — must match SAP, never silently drop.
6. **Treatment arm order** — Match randomization/sponsor order (typically Placebo → low dose → high dose as specified).
7. **Footnotes required:**

I'll map the raw demographics directly to the SDTM **DM** (Demographics) domain following SDTMIG v3.2/v3.3 conventions. No tools needed — answering from the domain knowledge above and CDISC standards.

---

# SDTM DM Domain Mapping: Raw Demographics → DM

## 1. Source-to-Target Variable Map

| DM Variable | Source | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| `STUDYID` | `study-config.yaml` → `study_id` | Constant across all records (e.g., `"ABC123"`) |
| `DOMAIN` | Constant | `"DM"` |
| `USUBJID` | `STUDYID` + `SITE` + `SUBJID` | `f"{STUDYID}-{SITE}-{SUBJID}"` (unique key) |
| `SUBJID` | `RAW.SUBJID` | Direct; strip site prefix if duplicated (see Edge Cases) |
| `SITEID` | `RAW.SITE` | Direct |
| `BRTHDTC` | `RAW.BRTHDAT` | ISO 8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD`) |
| `AGE` | `BRTHDAT`, reference date | Integer years BRTHDTC → reference date |
| `AGEU` | Constant | `"YEARS"` (CDISC CT C66781) |
| `SEX` | `RAW.SEX` | Map → CDISC CT C66731 |
| `RACE` | `RAW.RACE` | Map → CDISC CT C74488 |
| `ETHNIC` | `RAW.ETHNIC` | Map → CDISC CT C66344 |
| `ARMCD` | `RAW.TRTGRP` | Coded planned arm (Char ≤ 20) |
| `ARM` | `RAW.TRTGRP` | Decoded planned arm (Char ≤ 200) |
| `ACTARMCD` | `RAW.TRTGRP` | Defaults to `ARMCD` unless misrandomization |
| `ACTARM` | `RAW.TRTGRP` | Defaults to `ARM` unless misrandomization |
| `COUNTRY` | `RAW.COUNTRY` | ISO 3166-1 (3-letter) → CDISC CT C66766 |
| `DMDTC` | Collection date | ISO 8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD`) |
| `DMDY` | `DMDTC`, `RFSTDTC` | Study day of DM collection |

> `RFSTDTC`, `RFENDTC`, `RFXSTDTC`, `RFXENDTC`, `RFICDTC`, `RFPENDTC`, `DTHDTC`, `DTHFL`, `INVID` are populated from EX/DS/TV domains and aCRF; they are **not** derivable from this raw demographics block alone.

---

## 2. USUBJID Construction

```python
def derive_usubjid(study_id: str, site: str, subjid: str) -> str:
    """USUBJID = STUDYID-SITE-SUBJID, must be unique across the study."""
    return f"{study_id}-{site}-{subjid}"
```
- Example: `STUDYID="ABC123"`, `SITE="001"`, `SUBJID="001"` → `USUBJID="ABC123-001-001"`.
- Assert `USUBJID.is_unique` — DM must have **exactly one record per subject**.

---

## 3. AGE / AGEU Derivation

`AGE` = integer number of **completed years** from `BRTHDTC` to a reference date. The reference date must be **declared** (commonly `RFSTDTC` first study treatment, or `RFICDTC` informed consent — per SAP/study config).

```python
from datetime import date

def derive_age(brthdtc: str, ref_dt: date) -> int:
    """Age in completed years. Returns None if BRTHDTC missing/invalid."""
    if not brthdtc or len(brthdtc) < 10:
        return None
    b = date.fromisoformat(brthdtc[:10])
    age = ref_dt.year - b.year - ((ref_dt.month, ref_dt.day) < (b.month, b.day))
    if age < 0 or age > 120:   # sanity bounds
        raise ValueError(f"Implausible AGE {age} for BRTHDTC={brthdtc}")
    return age
```

- `AGEU = "YEARS"` whenever `AGE` is populated.
- If `BRTHDAT` is partial (e.g., `"1980-07"`), you cannot compute AGE → leave `AGE`/`AGEU` null and flag.
- Reference date stored in `study-config.yaml` (e.g., `age_reference: RFSTDTC`).

---

## 4. CDISC Controlled Terminology Mapping

### SEX (C66731)
| Raw input | DM `SEX` |
|---|---|
| M, MALE, M. | `M` |
| F, FEMALE, F. | `F` |
| UNDIFFERENTIATED | `UNDIFFERENTIATED` |
| unknown / blank | `U` |

### RACE (C74488)
| Raw input | DM `RACE` |
|---|---|
| white | `WHITE` |
| black, african american | `BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN` |
| asian | `ASIAN` |
| american indian, alaska native | `AMERICAN INDIAN OR ALASKA NATIVE` |
| native hawaiian, pacific islander | `NATIVE HAWAIIAN OR OTHER PACIFIC ISLANDER` |
| multiple | `MULTIPLE` |
| other | `OTHER` |
| unknown | `UNKNOWN` |
| not reported | `NOT REPORTED` |

### ETHNIC (C66344)
| Raw input | DM `ETHNIC` |
|---|---|
| hispanic, latino | `HISPANIC OR LATINO` |
| not hispanic | `NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO` |
| unknown | `UNKNOWN` |
| not reported | `NOT REPORTED` |

```python
SEX_MAP = {"M": "M", "MALE": "M", "F": "F", "FEMALE": "F",
           "UNDIFFERENTIATED": "UNDIFFERENTIATED"}
# RACE_MAP, ETHNIC_MAP analogous — key on normalized raw string

def normalize(s: str) -> str:
    return (s or "").strip().upper().replace(".", "").replace("_", " ")
```

---

## 5. ARM / ARMCD from TRTGRP

`ARMCD` rules (SDTMIG): ≤ 20 chars, **uppercase, alphanumeric, no spaces or special characters**, no lowercase, must not collide with reserved terms unless intended (`SCRNFAIL`, `NOTTRT`, `NOTASSGN`, `UNKN`).

Example sponsor mapping (driven by `study-config.yaml`):

| Raw `TRTGRP` | `ARMCD` | `ARM` |
|---|---|---|
| Placebo / Control | `PBO` | `Placebo` |
| Treatment 10 mg | `X10` | `Treatment X 10 mg` |
| Treatment 20 mg | `X20` | `Treatment X 20 mg` |
| Screen Failure | `SCRNFAIL` | `SCREEN FAILURE` |

```python
def derive_arm(raw_trtgrp: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Returns (ARMCD, ARM) from treatment mapping table."""
    key = normalize(raw_trtgrp)
    if key in {"SCREEN FAILURE", "SCRNFAIL", "SF"}:
        return "SCRNFAIL", "SCREEN FAILURE"
    if key not in ARM_MAP:
        raise ValueError(f"Unmapped TRTGRP: {raw_trtgrp!r}")
    return ARM_MAP[key]["ARMCD"], ARM_MAP[key]["ARM"]
```

- `ACTARMCD`/`ACTARM` default to `ARMCD`/`ARM` for correctly randomized, dosed subjects. Set `ACTARMCD="NOTTRT"`, `ACTARM="NOT TREATED"` for subjects randomized but never dosed; requires EX domain cross-check (deferred to `adam-adsl-builder`).

---

## 6. Full Build (Python)

```python
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path

def build_dm(raw_df: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, ref_dt) -> pd.DataFrame:
    study_id = cfg["study_id"]
    dm = pd.DataFrame()
    dm["STUDYID"] = study_id
    dm["DOMAIN"]  = "DM"
    dm["USUBJID"] = raw_df.apply(
        lambda r: f"{study_id}-{r['SITE']}-{r['SUBJID']}", axis=1)
    dm["SUBJID"]  = raw_df["SUBJID"]
    dm["SITEID"]  = raw_df["SITE"]
    dm["BRTHDTC"] = raw_df["BRTHDAT"].astype(str)         # assume ISO
    dm["AGE"]     = raw_df["BRTHDAT"].apply(lambda d: derive_age(d, ref_dt))
    dm["AGEU"]    = dm["AGE"].apply(lambda a: "YEARS" if pd.notna(a) else None)
    dm["SEX"]     = raw_df["SEX"].apply(lambda v: SEX_MAP.get(normalize(v), "U"))
    dm["RACE"]    = raw_df["RACE"].apply(lambda v: RACE_MAP.get(normalize(v), "UNKNOWN"))
    dm["ETHNIC"]  = raw_df["ETHNIC"].apply(lambda v: ETHNIC_MAP.get(normalize(v), "UNKNOWN"))
    dm[["ARMCD","ARM"]] = raw_df["TRTGRP"].apply(derive_arm).tolist()
    dm["ACTARMCD"] = dm["ARMCD"]
    dm["ACTARM"]   = dm["ARM"]
    dm["COUNTRY"]  = raw_df["COUNTRY"].str.upper()
    dm["DMDTC"]    = raw_df["DMDAT"].astype(str)          # collection date
    dm["DMDY"]     = None                                 # set vs RFSTDTC downstream

    assert dm["USUBJID"].is_unique, "DM: duplicate USUBJID"
    return dm
```

---

## 7. DM Output Schema (key columns)

| Variable | Type | Length | Core |
|---|---|---|---|
| STUDYID | Char | 22 | Req |
| DOMAIN | Char | 2 | Req |
| USUBJID | Char | 22 | Req |
| SUBJID | Char | 16 | Exp |
| SITEID | Char | 8 | Exp |
| BRTHDTC | Char | 10 | Perm |
| AGE | Num | 8 | Exp |
| AGEU | Char | 6 | Exp |
| SEX | Char | 2 | Exp |
| RACE | Char | 40 | Exp |
| ETHNIC | Char | 22 | Exp |
| ARMCD | Char | 20 | Req |
| ARM | Char | 200 | Req |
| ACTARMCD | Char | 20 | Req |
| ACTARM | Char | 200 | Req |
| COUNTRY | Char | 3 | Exp |

---

## 8. Edge Cases

| Scenario | Action |
|---|---|
| `SUBJID` already contains site prefix (`"SITE-001"`) | Keep raw in `SUBJID`; build `USUBJID` from clean SITE+SUBJID; document normalization |
| Missing/partial `BRTHDAT` (`"1980-07"`) | `AGE`/`AGEU` = null; flag in data review |
| Unmapped `TRTGRP` | **Abort build** — ARM/ARMCD must not be guessed; raise error |
| Duplicate `USUBJID` | Hard fail; DM must be 1 record/subject |
| Subject not in any treatment group | Only `SCRNFAIL` is a valid missing-treatment value |
| Implausible AGE (<0 or >120) | Reject and source-query before finalization |
| `SEX`/`RACE`/`ETHNIC` not in CT | Map to `U`/`UNKNOWN`/`UNKNOWN` only if genuinely unknown; otherwise reject |

```python
def generate_demographics_shell(adsl, treatment_var='TRT01P'):
    """
    Demographics table from ADSL.
    Continuous: AGE  -> n, Mean (SD), Median, Min-Max
    Categorical: SEX, RACE -> n (%)
    N values dynamically computed per treatment arm + total.
    """
    arms = ['Placebo', 'Drug 100mg', 'Drug 200mg']
    results = {}

    # ---- N header values (denominators) ----
    n_headers = {}
    for arm in arms + ['Total']:
        mask = (adsl[treatment_var] == arm) & (adsl['SAFFL'] == 'Y') \
               if arm != 'Total' else (adsl['SAFFL'] == 'Y')
        n_headers[arm] = int(mask.sum())

    # ---- Age (continuous) ----
    age = {}
    for arm in arms + ['Total']:
        subset = adsl.loc[
            (adsl[treatment_var] == arm) & (adsl['SAFFL'] == 'Y'), 'AGE'
        ].dropna() if arm != 'Total' else \
            adsl.loc[adsl['SAFFL'] == 'Y', 'AGE'].dropna()

        age[arm] = {
            'n': len(subset),
            'mean_sd': f"{subset.mean():.1f} ({subset.std(ddof=1):.2f})",
            'median': f"{subset.median():.1f}",
            'range': f"{subset.min():.0f}-{subset.max():.0f}",
        }

    # ---- Sex / Race (categorical) ----
    def categorical(var):
        out = {}
        for arm in arms + ['Total']:
            grp = adsl.loc[
                (adsl[treatment_var] == arm) & (adsl['SAFFL'] == 'Y')
            ] if arm != 'Total' else adsl.loc[adsl['SAFFL'] == 'Y']
            denom = len(grp)
            counts = grp[var].value_counts()
            out[arm] = {
                cat: {
                    'n': int(counts.get(cat, 0)),
                    'pct': (counts.get(cat, 0) / denom * 100) if denom else 0.0,
                }
                for cat in counts.index
            }
        return out

    results['n_headers'] = n_headers
    results['AGE'] = age
    results['SEX'] = categorical('SEX')
    results['RACE'] = categorical('RACE')
    return results
```

## Formatting & Precision Rules Applied

| Variable | Statistic | Precision | Example |
|----------|-----------|-----------|---------|
| AGE | n | integer | `42` |
| AGE | Mean (SD) | mean 1 dp, SD 2 dp in parens | `45.3 (11.27)` |
| AGE | Median | 1 decimal | `46.0` |
| AGE | Min–Max | integer | `19–74` |
| SEX | n (%) | n integer, % 1 dp | `28 (46.7)` |
| RACE | n (%) | n integer, % 1 dp | `45 (75.0)` |

- **Zero-count categories** (e.g., a race with no subjects) are still displayed as `0 (0.0)` — not suppressed.

## 1. Shell Layout

```
Safety Population

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Subjects with any AE                            XX (XX.X)      XX (XX.X)      ...        XX (XX.X)

(continued on next page if rows exceed 35 per page; headers repeat)
```

> Column headers are **dynamically derived** from `study-config.treatment_arms`; the `N=XXX` values are computed at runtime, never hardcoded.

---

## 2. Column Specification

| Column | Source | Align | N (denominator) |
|--------|--------|-------|------------------|
| Treatment arms (`{Arm 1}…{Arm K}`) | `study-config.treatment_arms`, keyed on `ADSL.TRT01P` | center | Safety pop. per arm |
| Total | Union of arms | center | Total safety pop. |

---

## 3. Row Derivation Logic

All counts are **distinct subjects (`USUBJID`)** within the safety population (`SAFFL='Y'`), grouped by `TRT01P`.

| # | Row | Filter (ADAE) | Denominator | Statistic |
|---|-----|---------------|-------------|-----------|
| 1 | Any AE | any record in ADAE (subject has ≥1 AE) | Safety N | n, n/N×100 |
| 2 | Treatment-emergent AE | `TRTEMFL = 'Y'` | Safety N | n, n/N×100 |
| 3 | Serious AE | `AESER = 'Y'` | Safety N | n, n/N×100 |
| 4 | AEs by severity | `ASEV` at subject's **maximum** severity | Safety N | n, n/N×100 |

**Severity block** — order Mild → Moderate → Severe. Each subject is counted **once** at their highest observed severity within that arm (so severity rows sum to ≤ "subjects with any TEAE").

```python
# Subject-level derivation skeleton
for trt in safety_arms:                      # TRT01P levels
    N = adsl_safety[adsl_safety.TRT01P==trt].USUBJID.nunique()
    any_ae   = adae_safe[adae_safe.TRT01P==trt].USUBJID.nunique()
    teae     = adae_safe.query("TRT01P==@trt and TRTEMFL=='Y'").USUBJID.nunique()
    ser      = adae_safe.query("TRT01P==@trt and AESER=='Y'").USUBJID.nunique()
    maxsev   = adae_safe.query("TRT01P==@trt and TRTEMFL=='Y'"
                               ).groupby("USUBJID").ASEV.max().value_counts()
    # report n (n/N*100) for each; ASEV ordinal: MILD < MODERATE < SEVERE
```

---

## 4. Required Variables & Data Gaps ⚠️

The provided ADAE spec `(TRT01P, TRTEMFL, AESER)` is **insufficient** for rows 1, 4, and the column denominator. Add:

| Dataset | Variable | Purpose | Status |
|---------|----------|---------|--------|
| ADAE | `USUBJID` | distinct-subject counting | **required** |
| ADAE | `ASEV` (analysis severity) | severity block (row 4) | **required — missing** |
| ADAE | `SAFFL` | restrict to safety population | **required — missing** |
| ADSL | `TRT01P`, `SAFFL` | column denominator N per arm | **required — external source** |

Without `ASEV`, the severity block **cannot be produced** — confirm the SAP severity/intensity variable (ADaM standard is `ASEV`; legacy SDTM uses `AESEV`) and add it to ADAE before programming.

**SAP-clarification flags (resolve before build):**
- *Any AE* (row 1): does it include **non-treatment-emergent** AEs, or only TEAEs? (Current shell treats "any AE" = all records; row 2 isolates TEAEs.)
- *Serious AE* (row 3): restrict to **treatment-emergent serious AEs** (`TRTEMFL='Y' AND AESER='Y'`)? Most SAPs do — confirm.
- Add **p-value column** (CMH or Fisher's exact) if SAP requires inferential comparison.

---

## 5. Footnotes (required, in order)

1. Protocol: {study_id}
2. Population: Safety (`SAFFL = 'Y'`)
3. Source: ADAE dataset
4. N = number of subjects in the safety population in the treatment group.

9. Data cutoff: {data_cut_date}

---

## 6. Decimal Precision

| Statistic | Precision |
|-----------|-----------|
| N, n | integer |
| % | 1 decimal (`XX.X`) |
| (p-value if added) | 4 decimals |

Format `n (%)` → `"XX (XX.X)"`. Do not pad zeros inconsistently (matches comparator normalization rules).

---

## 7. QC / Double-Programming Notes

- **Independent QC** must use separate code (ideally different language, e.g. SAS vs Python) on the same ADAE/ADSL + `table-specs.yaml`.
- Comparator tolerance: counts `0` (exact), percentages `0.1`, align by row label not position.
- Verify column N matches ADSL safety denominators (most common source of mismatch).

# SDTM AE Domain Mapping

Below is the complete mapping of raw adverse-event variables to the SDTM **AE** (Adverse Events) general-observation class domain, with derivation logic, controlled terminology, and ISO 8601 handling rules.

---

## 1. Identifier & Topic Variables (required for every AE record)

| Target Variable | Source | Derivation |
|-----------------|--------|------------|
| `STUDYID` | study config | Assigned — study identifier (e.g., `"ABC-123"`) |
| `DOMAIN` | constant | `"AE"` |
| `USUBJID` | DM | Concatenation of `STUDYID-SITEID-SUBJID` (lookup from DM) |
| `AESEQ` | derived | Sequential integer per subject (`order by AESTDTC, AETERM`) |
| `AESPID` | sponsor ID | Sponsor-defined identifier (often raw row ID) |
| `AETERM` | `AETERM_RAW` | Verbatim term, as reported. Trim/normalize whitespace; do not correct spelling. |

---

## 2. AETERM, AEDECOD (MedDRA Coding) & AEBODSYS

```
AETERM   = trim(AETERM_RAW)                      # verbatim, untouched
AEDECOD  = MedDRA_PT(AETERM)                     # Preferred Term from MedDRA auto-encoder
AEBODSYS = MedDRA_SOC(AEDECOD)                   # Primary System Organ Class (LLT→PT→SOC)
AELLT    = MedDRA_LLT(AETERM)                    # (optional) Lowest Level Term
```

**Rules:**
- `AEDECOD` is the **Preferred Term (PT)** assigned by the MedDRA dictionary (current version, e.g., MedDRA 26.x / 27.x — must be locked for the study).
- `AEBODSYS` is **NOT** a separate raw value — it is the **Primary SOC** derived from the PT via the MedDRA hierarchy (`LLT → PT → SOC`). For multi-SOC PTs, use the **primary SOC** flag from the dictionary.
- If `AETERM` is unmappable, set `AEDECOD = ""` and flag for medical review (do **not** populate with a synthetic value).
- `AETERM` must remain verbatim; corrections to spelling happen only via the MedDRA auto-encoder mapping table.

---

## 3. AESTDTC, AEENDTC (ISO 8601 Date Conversion)

```
AESTDTC = ISO8601(AESTDAT)
AEENDTC = ISO8601(AEENDAT)
```

**ISO 8601 formatting rules:**

| Raw form | ISO 8601 output | Notes |
|----------|-----------------|-------|
| `15MAR2023` (complete) | `2023-03-15` | Full date |
| `MAR2023` (month/year only) | `2023-03` | Partial — keep precision |
| `2023` (year only) | `2023` | Partial |
| `UNK MAR 2023` | `2023-03` | Drop unknown component, keep known precision |
| `UNK UNK 2023` | `2023` | |
| Missing / all unknown | `""` (blank) | Leave blank — never fabricate |

- Convert DDMONYYYY → `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- **Preserve partial precision** — never pad unknown day/month with `01` or impute. Imputation flags (`*STDTC` companion variables) belong in **ADaM** (e.g., `ASTDTMF`), not in SDTM.
- Datetimes, if time component exists → `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss` (SDTM allows `--DTC` to carry time if collected).

---

## 4. AESEV, AESER, AEREL (Controlled Terminology)

### AESEV (Severity / Intensity)
Mapped to **CDISC CT** (NCI EVS) — case-sensitive, exact match required:

| Raw `AESEV` value | `AESEV` (CT) |
|-------------------|--------------|
| MILD / 1 | `MILD` |
| MODERATE / 2 | `MODERATE` |
| SEVERE / 3 | `SEVERE` |

> Per SDTM IG, severity = investigator-assessed **intensity**, independent of seriousness. Keep the controlled-term casing exactly as `MILD/MODERATE/SEVERE`.

### AESER (Seriousness Indicator)
Single character flag (`Y`/`null`), CT-compliant:

```
AESER = if AESER_RAW in ("YES","Y","1",1) then "Y"
        else ""                            # leave blank — do NOT write "N"
```

- SDTM CT value: `Y` if serious, **blank otherwise** (do not populate `N`).
- Seriousness must align with the regulatory criteria (death, life-threatening, hospitalization, etc.). If the raw form captures individual criteria (AESDTH, AESLIFE, etc.), those populate separate Supplemental or standard AE qualifiers where applicable.

### AEREL (Causality — Relationship to Study Treatment)
CT-aligned values (sponsor-specific; commonly):

| Raw value | `AEREL` |
|-----------|---------|
| Related / YES / 1 | `RELATED` (or `Y` per sponsor CT) |
| Not Related / NO / 0 | `NOT RELATED` (or `N`) |
| Possibly / Probably | Map to sponsor-defined CT values |

> AEREL CT is frequently sponsor-specific; confirm against the study's CRF annotation and CT package before finalizing.

---

## 5. Recommended Companion Qualifiers (standard AE completeness)

These are standard AE variables that should be present even if not listed in the raw set — populate from raw if available, otherwise leave blank pending data:

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `AEOUT` | Outcome (RECOVERED/RECOVERING/NOT RECOVERED/RECOVERED WITH SEQUELAE/FATAL/UNKNOWN) |
| `AEREL` | Causality (above) |
| `AEACN` | Action taken with study treatment |
| `AEPREL` | Pre-existing flag (Y) |
| `AECONTRT` | Concomitant treatment given (Y) |
| `AETOXGR` | Toxicity grade (CTCAE, if graded) |
| `AESDTH, AESLIFE, AESHOSP, AESDISAB, AESCONG, AESMIE` | Seriousness criteria flags (Y) — if individually collected |

---

## 6. Mapping Pseudocode (consolidated)

```python
def map_ae(raw, study, dm, meddra):
    return {
        "STUDYID":  study.id,
        "DOMAIN":   "AE",
        "USUBJID":  dm_usubjid(raw.SUBJID, dm),
        "AESEQ":    next_seq(raw.USUBJID),
        "AESPID":   raw.SPID,
        "AETERM":   norm_space(raw.AETERM_RAW),
        "AEDECOD":  meddra.pt(raw.AETERM_RAW),       # PT
        "AEBODSYS": meddra.primary_soc(meddra.pt(raw.AETERM_RAW)),  # SOC
        "AESTDTC":  iso8601(raw.AESTDAT, preserve_partial=True),
        "AEENDTC":  iso8601(raw.AEENDAT, preserve_partial=True),
        "AESEV":    map_severity_ct(raw.AESEV),      # MILD/MODERATE/SEVERE
        "AESER":    "Y" if truthy(raw.AESER) else "",  # blank, never "N"
        "AEREL":    map_relation_ct(raw.AEREL),
    }
```

---

## 7. Edge Cases & QC Notes

- **Missing AEENDAT with AESTDAT present** → `AEENDTC` blank; do not infer. Ongoing events are typically flagged later in ADaM (`AENDY`, ongoing flag), not imputed in SDTM.
- **Same AETERM recurring** → each occurrence is a separate AE record (distinct `AESEQ`); do not collapse.
- **AETERM not yet coded** → `AEDECOD`/`AEBODSYS` blank; track as a data clarification query.
- **Date components UNK** → keep the known portion at its natural ISO 8601 precision; never pad.
- **Duplicate (AESTDTC, AETERM) within subject** → flag for reconciliation before assigning `AESEQ`.
- **Severity vs. seriousness** are independent — do not derive one from the other.

---

📋 **Operation Review**
1. Mapped all six raw AE variables to SDTM AE targets, with `AEBODSYS` derived via MedDRA SOC and `AESER`/`AESEV` converted to CDISC CT.
2. Provided ISO 8601 partial-date handling, causality CT mapping, companion qualifier list, consolidated pseudocode, and edge-case/QC notes.

📊 **Current Status**
• Output is a specification/derivation reference — no files written.

💡 **Next Steps**
1. Confirm the locked **MedDRA version** and the study-specific **AEREL CT** codelist before finalizing.
2. Add serious-criteria flags (AESDTH, AESHOSP, …) if the CRF collects them individually.
3. Run P21 validation (`/p21-validator`) on the resulting `ae.xpt` to verify CT and IG conformance.

# ADAE Derivation (AE + ADSL)

Below is a complete, production-grade derivation of **TRTEMFL, ASTDT/AENDT, AOCCFL, AOCCPFL, and ADURN**, following the `adam-adae-builder` skill logic. The dataset is **1 record per AE** (1:many with ADSL); treatment/population fields are inherited from ADSL via a left-merge on `USUBJID`.

## Derivation logic (in execution order)

| # | Variable(s) | Rule | Source |
|---|-------------|------|--------|
| 1 | `ASTDT`, `AENDT` | Parse `AESTDTC`/`AEENDTC` with partial-date imputation. **Start** imputes to first plausible day (`-01`); **End** imputes to last plausible day (last-of-month / Dec 31) so duration is conservative. | Derived from AE |
| 2 | `ASTDY` | `(ASTDT − TRTSDT).days + 1`; null if either date missing. | Derived |
| 3 | `TRTEMFL` | Full TEAE definition (not just `AESTDTC ≥ TRTSDT`): `SAFFL≠'Y'→'N'`; missing ASTDT or TRTSDT → `''` (indeterminate); `ASTDT < TRTSDT` → `'N'` (pre-tx, **kept**); `ASTDT > TRTEDT + teae_window_days` → `'N'` (post-window, **kept**); otherwise `'Y'`. Same-day-as-TRTSDT → `'Y'`. | Derived |
| 4 | `AOCCFL` | First occurrence of **Preferred Term** (`AEDECOD`) within subject, among `TRTEMFL='Y'`, by earliest `ASTDT`. | Derived |
| 5 | `AOCCPFL` | First occurrence of **System Organ Class** (`AEBODSYS`) within subject, among `TRTEMFL='Y'`. ⚠ See caveat below. | Derived |
| 6 | `ADURN`, `ADTU` | `(AENDT − ASTDT).days + 1`; null if either date missing. `ADTU='DAYS'`. | Derived |

> **Note on TRTEMFL:** the task headline simplifies this to `AESTDTC ≥ TRTSDT`. The regulatory-correct TEAE flag *also* gates on the safety population and a post-treatment follow-up window (default 30 d, configurable). I implement the full definition; the `ASTDT ≥ TRTSDT` rule is the core inclusion branch.

## Code

```python
"""ADAE builder: derive ADAE from SDTM AE + ADSL.

Derivations:
  ASTDT / AENDT  analysis start/end dates (partial-date imputation)
  ASTDY          study day of AE start (ASTDT - TRTSDT + 1)
  TRTEMFL        treatment-emergent AE flag
  AOCCFL         first occurrence of Preferred Term (AEDECOD) among TEAEs
  AOCCPFL        first occurrence of System Organ Class (AEBODSYS) among TEAEs
  ADURN / ADTU   AE duration in days

One ADAE record per AE; ADSL merged 1:many on USUBJID.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import calendar
import logging
from datetime import date
from typing import Optional

import pandas as pd

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_TEAE_WINDOW_DAYS_DEFAULT = 30


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Date derivations
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _last_day_of_month(year: int, month: int) -> date:
    """Return the last calendar day of (year, month)."""
    last = calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]
    return date(year, month, last)


def _is_blank(value: object) -> bool:
    return value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and pd.isna(value)) or str(value).strip() == ""


def to_start_date(dtc: Optional[str]) -> Optional[date]:
    """Parse an ISO --DTC string, imputing to the FIRST plausible day.

    missing -> None | YYYY-MM-DD -> as-is | YYYY-MM -> -01 | YYYY -> -01-01.
    """
    if _is_blank(dtc):
        return None
    s = str(dtc).strip()
    try:
        if len(s) >= 10:
            return date.fromisoformat(s[:10])
        if len(s) == 7:
            return date.fromisoformat(s + "-01")
        if len(s) == 4:
            return date.fromisoformat(s + "-01-01")
    except ValueError:
        logger.warning("Unparseable start --DTC %r; treated as missing", dtc)
        return None
    logger.warning("Unexpected --DTC length %r; treated as missing", dtc)
    return None


def to_end_date(dtc: Optional[str]) -> Optional[date]:
    """Parse an end --DTC string, imputing to the LAST plausible day.

    YYYY-MM -> last day of month | YYYY -> Dec 31 (conservative for duration).
    """
    if _is_blank(dtc):
        return None
    s = str(dtc).strip()
    try:
        if len(s) >= 10:
            return date.fromisoformat(s[:10])
        if len(s) == 7:
            return _last_day_of_month(int(s[0:4]), int(s[5:7]))
        if len(s) == 4:
            return date(int(s), 12, 31)
    except (ValueError, IndexError):
        logger.warning("Unparseable end --DTC %r; treated as missing", dtc)
        return None
    return None


def derive_dates(adae: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Derive ASTDT (start-imputed) and AENDT (end-imputed) as datetime64[ns]."""
    adae["ASTDT"] = pd.to_datetime(adae["AESTDTC"].map(to_start_date), errors="coerce")
    adae["AENDT"] = pd.to_datetime(adae["AEENDTC"].map(to_end_date), errors="coerce")
    return adae


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# TRTEMFL
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def derive_trtemfl(adae: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Treatment-emergent AE flag.

    '' = indeterminate | 'N' = non-emergent (record KEPT) | 'Y' = emergent.
    Window length comes from cfg['teae_window_days'] (default 30); never hardcoded.
    """
    window = int(cfg.get("teae_window_days", _TEAE_WINDOW_DAYS_DEFAULT))

    saffl = adae["SAFFL"].fillna("").eq("Y")
    astdt, trtsdt, trtedt = adae["ASTDT"], adae["TRTSDT"], adae["TRTEDT"]
    has_dates = astdt.notna() & trtsdt.notna()

    flag = pd.Series("Y", index=adae.index, dtype=object)        # default emergent
    flag[~saffl] = "N"                                           # not in safety population
    flag[saffl & ~has_dates] = ""                                # indeterminate
    flag[saffl & has_dates & astdt.lt(trtsdt)] = "N"             # pre-treatment
    post_window = (
        saffl & has_dates & trtedt.notna()
        & astdt.gt(trtedt + pd.Timedelta(days=window))
    )
    flag[post_window] = "N"                                      # beyond follow-up window

    adae["TRTEMFL"] = flag
    return adae


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# First-occurrence flags (AOCCFL, AOCCPFL)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _first_occurrence_flag(
    df: pd.DataFrame, group_cols: list[str], flag_name: str
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag 'Y' on the earliest treatment-emergent record per group; else 'N'.

    Considers only TRTEMFL == 'Y' records; sorts by ASTDT (NaT last).
    """
    df[flag_name] = "N"
    teae = df.loc[df["TRTEMFL"] == "Y"]
    if teae.empty:
        return df
    ordered = teae.sort_values(group_cols + ["ASTDT"], na_position="last")
    first_rows = ordered.groupby(group_cols, dropna=False, sort=False).head(1)
    df.loc[first_rows.index, flag_name] = "Y"
    return df


def derive_occurrence_flags(adae: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    # AOCCFL  : first occurrence of Preferred Term (AEDECOD)
    _first_occurrence_flag(adae, ["USUBJID", "AEDECOD"], "AOCCFL")
    # AOCCPFL : first occurrence of System Organ Class (AEBODSYS)
    _first_occurrence_flag(adae, ["USUBJID", "AEBODSYS"], "AOCCPFL")
    return adae


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Duration
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def derive_adurn(adae: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """ADURN = (AENDT - ASTDT).days + 1; null if either date missing."""
    dur = (adae["AENDT"] - adae["ASTDT"]).dt.days + 1
    adae["ADURN"] = dur.astype("Int64")
    adae["ADTU"] = "DAYS"

    bad = adae["ADURN"].notna() & (adae["ADURN"] <= 0)
    if bad.any():
        logger.warning("%d record(s) have AENDT < ASTDT (ADURN <= 0); review dates", int(bad.sum()))
    return adae


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Build
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def build_adae(ae: pd.DataFrame, adsl: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Merge AE with ADSL (1:many on USUBJID) and run all derivations.

    Args:
        ae:   SDTM AE domain (one row per adverse event).
        adsl: ADSL subject-level dataset (carries TRTP/TRTA/SAFFL/TRTSDT/TRTEDT).
        cfg:  derivation config; key `teae_window_days` (int, default 30).

    Returns:
        ADAE analysis dataset.
    """
    logger.info("Building ADAE: AE rows=%d, ADSL subjects=%d",
                len(ae), adsl["USUBJID"].nunique())

    adsl_cols = ["USUBJID"] + [
        c for c in ("TRTP", "TRTA", "SAFFL", "TRTSDT", "TRTEDT") if c in adsl.columns
    ]
    adae = ae.merge(adsl[adsl_cols], on="USUBJID", how="left", suffixes=("", "_ADSL"))

    if adae["USUBJID"].isna().any():
        raise ValueError("Merge produced missing USUBJID; verify AE/ADSL key integrity")

    orphans = adae["SAFFL"].isna()
    if orphans.any():
        # Per skill constraint: NEVER drop orphans — keep and flag for review.
        logger.warning("%d AE record(s) have no matching ADSL subject (kept for review)",
                       int(orphans.sum()))

    # Normalize ADSL date columns to datetime64 for vectorized arithmetic.
    for col in ("TRTSDT", "TRTEDT"):
        if col in adae.columns:
            adae[col] = pd.to_datetime(adae[col], errors="coerce")

    derive_dates(adae)
    adae["ASTDY"] = ((adae["ASTDT"] - adae["TRTSDT"]).dt.days + 1).astype("Int64")

    derive_trtemfl(adae, cfg)
    derive_occurrence_flags(adae)
    derive_adurn(adae)

    logger.info("ADAE built: %d rows | TEAE=%d | AOCCFL='Y'=%d",
                len(adae), int((adae["TRTEMFL"] == "Y").sum()),
                int((adae["AOCCFL"] == "Y").sum()))
    return adae
```

**Driver (matches the skill CLI):**

```bash
adam-adae-builder --input-dir output/sdtm --output output/adam/adae.xpt \
  --adsl output/adam/adsl.xpt --spec specs/adam-spec.yaml --validate
```

`cfg` is read from `specs/adam-spec.yaml`; the only key consumed here is `teae_window_days`.

## Edge cases handled

| Scenario | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| Missing `AESTDTC` | `ASTDT=NaT`; `TRTEMFL=''` (indeterminate); record **kept** |
| Partial start date (`YYYY-MM` / `YYYY`) | Impute day = 01 |
| Partial end date (`YYYY-MM` / `YYYY`) | Impute to last-of-month / Dec 31 |
| Pre-treatment AE | `TRTEMFL='N'`; record kept; excluded from occurrence flags |
| Duplicate AE (same PT, same day) | All kept; `AOCCFL='Y'` on exactly one |
| Missing `AEDECOD` | Grouped with `dropna=False`; flagged for review (AETERM fallback per spec) |
| AE with no ADSL match (orphan) | **Kept**; logged — never dropped |
| `AENDT < ASTDT` | `ADURN ≤ 0`; logged for review |
| Same-day start as TRTSDT | `TRTEMFL='Y'` (treatment-emergent) |

## ⚠️ Caveat on AOCCPFL

`AOCCPFL` is **not** a CDISC-IG-canonical variable the way `AOCCFL` is, so its exact meaning is study-specific. I implemented the **analytically standard companion**: first occurrence of **AEBODSYS (System Organ Class)**, which lets you count *subjects once per SOC* in "AE by SOC and PT" tables without double-counting (a subject with two different PTs in one SOC has two `AOCCFL='Y'` rows but one `AOCCPFL='Y'`).

If your `specs/adam-spec.yaml` instead defines `AOCCPFL` as PT-level (e.g., "Preferred-term occurrence"), it would be **identical** to `AOCCFL` — in which case point it at `["USUBJID","AEDECOD"]`. **Confirm the definition against the SAP / ADaM spec before submission.**

## Verification checklist (before sign-off)

- [ ] `adae["USUBJID"].notna().all()`
- [ ] No records dropped vs. source AE (row count = AE rows)
- [ ] `TRTEMFL ∈ {"", "N", "Y"}`; `""` only where ASTDT or TRTSDT missing
- [ ] `AOCCFL` has exactly one `'Y'` per `(USUBJID, AEDECOD)` among TEAEs
- [ ] `ADURN` null iff `ASTDT` or `AENDT` missing
- [ ] `teae_window_days` sourced from cfg, not hardcoded

---

📋 **Operation Review**
1. Derived ADAE from AE + ADSL: merged 1:many on `USUBJID`, then derived dates → study day → TRTEMFL → AOCCFL/AOCCPFL → ADURN.
2. No files modified (single self-contained derivation module provided above).

📊 **Current Status**
- Logic ready to drop into `adam-adae-builder`; aligns with skill constraints (no orphans dropped, cfg-driven window, no blind dedupe, imputation documented).

💡 **Next Steps**
1. Paste into the builder module, wire `cfg` from `specs/adam-spec.yaml`, run `--validate`.
2. Confirm `AOCCPFL` semantics against the SAP/ADaM spec (SOC vs PT).
3. Run `/adam-traceability-checker` and `/adam-validator` (P21) on the produced `adae.xpt`.

## 2. Structural Spec (feeds `tfl-table-generator`)

```yaml
table_output:
  table_id: "Table 14.1.3"
  title: "Demographics and Baseline Characteristics by Treatment Group (Safety Population)"
  population: "SAFFL"
  population_name: "Safety Population"
  population_flag: "SAFFL"
  source_dataset: "ADSL"
  treatment_var: "TRT01P"
  format: "rtf"
  orientation: "Landscape"

  columns:
    - label: ""                          # row-label column, left-aligned
      align: "left"
    - label: "Placebo"
      sublabel: "(N={count Placebo})"
      align: "center"
    - label: "Drug 100mg"
      sublabel: "(N={count Drug 100mg})"
      align: "center"
    - label: "Drug 200mg"
      sublabel: "(N={count Drug 200mg})"
      align: "center"
    - label: "Total"
      sublabel: "(N={count total})"
      align: "center"

  rows:
    - block: "Age (years)"
      type: "continuous"
      variable: "AGE"
      statistics: ["n", "Mean (SD)", "Median", "Range"]

    - block: "Sex"
      type: "categorical"
      variable: "SEX"
      statistic: "n (%)"
      category_order: ["F", "M"]                 # alphabetical per SAP default
      show_missing: true

    - block: "Race"
      type: "categorical"
      variable: "RACE"
      statistic: "n (%)"
      category_order:                             # CDISC/NCI standard, SAP-defined
        - "AMERICAN INDIAN OR ALASKA NATIVE"
        - "ASIAN"
        - "BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN"
        - "NATIVE HAWAIIAN OR OTHER PACIFIC ISLANDER"
        - "WHITE"
        - "OTHER"
      show_missing: true
```

---

## 3. Decimal Precision Applied

| Variable | Statistic | Format | Example |
|----------|-----------|--------|---------|
| AGE (continuous) | n | integer | `42` |
| | Mean | 1 decimal | `54.3` |
| | SD | 2 decimals, in parentheses after Mean | `(11.27)` |
| | Median | 1 decimal | `55.0` |
| | Range | integer min–max | `23–78` |
| SEX, RACE (categorical) | n | integer | `18` |
| | % | 1 decimal, in parentheses after n | `(48.6)` |

- **Column percentages** — denominator = treatment-group N (subjects in `SAFFL='Y'` within each `TRT01P` arm), not the row total.
- **No p-values / no formal hypothesis testing** in this shell — the task did not request comparative inference. If the SAP requires it, add a `p-value` column using ANCOVA (AGE) and CMH (SEX, RACE); p-values to **4 decimals**.

---

## 4. Required Footnotes (in mandated order)

```
Protocol: {study_id}
Population: Safety (SAFFL = 'Y')
Source: ADSL dataset
N = number of subjects in the treatment group (Safety Population).
Age was derived from ADSL.AGE; treatment from ADSL.TRT01P.
Percentages are calculated within treatment group (column percentages).
Data cutoff: {data_cut_date}
```

---

## 5. Edge-Case Rules (apply during generation)

- **Zero counts** — still render the row as `0 (0.0%)`; never suppress a collected category.
- **Small cell sizes (<5)** — display `n (%)` as-is; if p-values are later added, switch from CMH to **Fisher's exact**.
- **Missing data** — if any variable has **>5% missing**, add a footnote: *"X% of subjects had missing {VARIABLE}."*
- **Multi-page** — repeat title (with `(continued)`), column headers, and N-row on every page; `Page X of Y` bottom-center; max 35 rows/page.
- **Arm name mismatch** — resolve arm labels (`Placebo`, `Drug 100mg`, `Drug 200mg`) from `study-config.treatment_arms`, **never hardcode** ARMCD values.

2. Run generator → `output/tfl/tables/table-14.1.3-demographics.rtf`, then `/tfl-double-programmer` for independent QC.

# SDTM DM Mapping — Raw Demographics → DM Domain

Below is the complete derivation mapping each raw variable to its SDTM DM target, using CDISC SDTM IG v2.x conventions. I'll address the four required mappings, add the standard DM identifier/date variables needed to make the dataset valid, then provide controlled-terminology (CT) reference tables, a derivation snippet, and edge cases.

---

## 0. Required DM Record Identifiers (set every record)

| DM Variable | Source | Derivation |
|-------------|--------|------------|
| `STUDYID` | study config | Sponsor study identifier, e.g. `"XYZ-123"` |
| `DOMAIN` | constant | `"DM"` |
| `USUBJID` | derived | `STUDYID-SITEID-SUBJID` (see §1) |
| `SUBJID` | RAW `SUBJID` | Subject number within site |
| `SITEID` | RAW `SITE` | Site number (e.g., `"001"`) |
| `RFSTDTC` | EX / study config | Reference start date (first dose or randomization per SAP) — needed for AGE |
| `RFENDTC` | DS / study config | Reference end date |

---

## 1. USUBJID = STUDYID-SITEID-SUBJID

`USUBJID` must be **unique across the entire study** and must be the concatenation of `STUDYID`, `SITEID`, and `SUBJID` with `-` separators.

```python
SITEID = str(raw.SITE).zfill(3)          # "001"
SUBJID = str(raw.SUBJID)                  # subject-within-site number
USUBJID = f"{study_id}-{SITEID}-{SUBJID}" # "XYZ-123-001-0014"
```

**Important interpretation note on the raw `SUBJID(SITE-001)`:**
The raw token `SITE-001` looks like a *site-qualified* value. In SDTM you must split, not reuse verbatim:
- If `SUBJID` already contains the site prefix (e.g., `"SITE-001"`), strip the site portion and keep only the subject sequence for `SUBJID`, taking the site portion for `SITEID`. Do **not** let `SUBJID` redundantly carry `SITEID`, or `USUBJID` will look like `XYZ-123-001-SITE-001`.
- Validate `USUBJID` uniqueness (`assert dm["USUBJID"].is_unique`).

---

## 2. AGE / AGEU from BRTHDAT

`AGE` is the **integer number of completed years** between `BRTHDAT` (birth date) and the reference date (`RFSTDTC`). `AGEU` is always `"YEARS"`.

```python
def derive_age(brthdat, rfstdtc):
    if not brthdat or not rfstdtc:
        return None
    delta = (parse(rfstdtc) - parse(brthdat)).days
    return int(delta // 365.25)        # completed years

AGE  = derive_age(raw.BRTHDAT, RFSTDTC)   # numeric
AGEU = "YEARS" if AGE is not None else ""
```

**Edge cases**
| Scenario | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Missing `BRTHDAT` | `AGE` = missing; flag for QC; do **not** impute |
| Missing reference date | Use the SAP-defined AGE reference (typically `RFSTDTC`); never use "today" |
| `BRTHDAT` after reference date | Data error — flag, do not emit negative AGE |
| Partial `BRTHDAT` (`YYYY-MM`) | Do not impute for AGE — birth date is too sensitive; flag instead |
| Subject < 1 year | Use whole months only if study is pediatric and AGEU permits; otherwise YEARS |

---

## 3. SEX / RACE / ETHNIC → CDISC CT

All three are **CDISC submission-value (CT)** variables. Map the raw collected text to the exact published extensible-CT submission values.

### SEX — CT C979197 (`Sex`)
| Raw collected | DM value |
|---|---|
| Male / M | `M` |
| Female / F | `F` |
| Unknown | `U` |
| Undifferentiated | `UNDIFFERENTIATED` |

### RACE — CT C74457 (`Race`)
| Raw collected | DM value |
|---|---|
| White | `WHITE` |
| Black or African American | `BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN` |
| Asian | `ASIAN` |
| American Indian / Alaska Native | `AMERICAN INDIAN OR ALASKA NATIVE` |
| Native Hawaiian / Other Pacific Islander | `NATIVE HAWAIIAN OR OTHER PACIFIC ISLANDER` |
| More than one race selected | `MULTIPLE` |
| Other (no listed option) | `OTHER` |
| Unknown | `UNKNOWN` |
| Not reported / refused | `NOT REPORTED` |

### ETHNIC — CT C16592 (`Ethnicity`)
| Raw collected | DM value |
|---|---|
| Hispanic or Latino | `HISPANIC OR LATINO` |
| Not Hispanic or Latino | `NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO` |
| Unknown | `UNKNOWN` |
| Not reported / refused | `NOT REPORTED` |

> Validate every output value against the current CDISC CT package; any non-matching value must be flagged — do **not** silently truncate or lowercase.

---

## 4. ARM / ARMCD from TRTGRP

`ARM` = full description of the **planned** arm; `ARMCD` = ≤20-char code, unique and stable per arm. Define the mapping once in the study config and apply it consistently.

| Raw `TRTGRP` | `ARMCD` | `ARM` |
|---|---|---|
| Placebo | `PBO` | `Placebo` |
| Treatment 10 mg | `DRUG 10` | `Treatment 10 mg` |
| Treatment 20 mg | `DRUG 20` | `Treatment 20 mg` |
| Active Comparator | `ACTIVE` | `Active Comparator` |
| Screen Failure | `SCRNFAIL` | `Screen Failure` |
| Not Assigned | `NOTASSGN` | `Not Assigned` |
| Not Treated | `NOTTRT` | `Not Treated` |

```python
ARM_MAP = study_config["arm_map"]   # {TRTGRP: (ARMCD, ARM)}
ARMCD, ARM = ARM_MAP.get(raw.TRTGRP, ("", ""))
```

**Actual treatment (set in parallel):**
- `ACTARM` / `ACTARMCD` = actual arm derived from `DM.ACTARM` or `EX` treatment actually received. For randomized-and-dosed subjects these usually equal `ARM`/`ARMCD`; for subjects never dosed, `ACTARM="NOT TREATED"` (`ACTARMCD="NOTTRT"`).

**Rules**
- `ARMCD` ≤ 20 chars, alphanumeric, no embedded blanks, unique across arms.
- `ARM` and `ARMCD` must be 1:1 consistent (every `ARMCD` maps to exactly one `ARM`).
- Screen failures keep `ARMCD="SCRNFAIL"`; they remain in DM (one record per subject) but are excluded from most analysis populations downstream.

---

## Worked Example Record

Assume `STUDYID="XYZ-123"`, `RFSTDTC="2026-01-15"`, and one raw row:

```
SUBJID=0014, SITE=001, BRTHDAT=1985-06-20, SEX=Female, RACE=White,
ETHNIC=Not Hispanic or Latino, TRTGRP=Treatment 10 mg, COUNTRY=USA
```

→ DM record:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `STUDYID` | `XYZ-123` |
| `DOMAIN` | `DM` |
| `USUBJID` | `XYZ-123-001-0014` |
| `SUBJID` | `0014` |
| `SITEID` | `001` |
| `AGE` | `40` |
| `AGEU` | `YEARS` |
| `SEX` | `F` |
| `RACE` | `WHITE` |
| `ETHNIC` | `NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO` |
| `ARMCD` | `DRUG 10` |
| `ARM` | `Treatment 10 mg` |
| `ACTARMCD` | `DRUG 10` |
| `ACTARM` | `Treatment 10 mg` |
| `COUNTRY` | `USA` |
| `RFSTDTC` | `2026-01-15` |

(`COUNTRY` uses ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 — `USA`; `BRTHDAT` is consumed for AGE only, it is **not** retained in DM.)

---

## Critical Constraints (compliance)

**Never**
- Reuse a site-qualified string verbatim as `SUBJID` — split site vs. subject.
- Emit negative or non-integer `AGE`; impute birth date.
- Assign `ARM`/`ARMCD` that violate the 1:1 rule or the 20-char `ARMCD` limit.
- Map raw race/sex/ethnicity text directly without normalizing to current CDISC CT.
- Drop screen-failure subjects from DM (they belong in DM with `ARMCD="SCRNFAIL"`).

**Always**
- Start DM as the 1-record-per-subject backbone; assert uniqueness of `USUBJID`.
- Resolve `STUDYID`, arm map, and AGE reference date from `study-config.yaml`.
- Keep `ARM`/`ACTARM` both populated and document any `ARM ≠ ACTARM`.
- Flag — never silently fix — unmappable CT values or missing birth/reference dates.

---

📋 **Operation Review**
1. Mapped 8 raw variables → SDTM DM, plus the standard identifier/date variables required for a valid record.
2. No files modified — this is a mapping specification (deliverable is the spec/derivation above).

📊 **Current Status**
• DM derivation rules fully specified for USUBJID, AGE/AGEU, SEX/RACE/ETHNIC CT, and ARM/ARMCD.
• CT tables reference current CDISC packages (Sex C979197, Race C74457, Ethnicity C16592).

💡 **Next Steps**
1. Encode `ARM_MAP`, `CT` maps, and the AGE reference date in `specs/study-config.yaml` and `specs/sdtm-mapping-spec.yaml`.
2. Implement the derivations in `/sdtm-dm-mapper`, then validate with `/sdtm-validator` and run P21 (`/p21-validator`) before downstream ADSL build (`/adam-adsl-builder`).
3. Cross-check that every DM subject propagates to ADSL (`USUBJID` 1:1) and that `ARMCD` values used here match the Treatment Arms defined in the Trial Design (TX) domains.

# ADSL Derivation from SDTM

Below is the complete derivation of the subject-level analysis dataset (**ADSL**) following ADaM IG v1.3 and the conventions in the `adam-adsl-builder` skill. ADSL maintains exactly **one record per subject**, with DM as the backbone and EX/DS left-joined.

## 1. Derivation Logic

### Core principle
ADSL is built by starting with **DM** (1:1 with subjects) and left-joining EX (dose dates) and DS (disposition). The cardinality invariant `len(ADSL) == len(DM)` with unique `USUBJID` must hold.

### Treatment assignment
| Variable | Source | Rule |
|----------|--------|------|
| `TRT01P` | `DM.ARM` | Planned treatment (verbatim from randomization) |
| `TRT01A` | `DM.ACTARM` (fallback `DM.ARM`) | Actual treatment received |

If `ARM != ACTARM` (dose modification / crossover), preserve both — never overwrite. Document the discrepancy.

### Treatment dates (from EX)
```python
# Restrict to records where a real dose was given
ex_dosed = ex[ex["EXDOSE"] > 0]
trt_dates = (
    ex_dosed.groupby("USUBJID")
            .agg(TRTSDT=("EXSTDTC", "min"),   # first dose date
                 TRTEDT=("EXENDTC", "max"))    # last dose date
            .reset_index()
)
adsl = dm.merge(trt_dates, on="USUBJID", how="left")
```
- Screen failures / never-dosed subjects → `TRTSDT = TRTEDT = null`.
- Impute partial `--STDTC` as start = day 01, end = last day of month.
- Enforce `TRTSDT <= TRTEDT` for all treated subjects (ADSL007).

### Population flags
```python
screen_code = study_config.get("screen_failure_code", "Scrnfail")

# ITTFL: randomized subject (assigned a non-screen-failure arm)
ITTFL = "Y" if ARMCD != screen_code else "N"

# SAFFL: randomized AND received at least one dose (EXDOSE > 0)
SAFFL = "Y" if (ARMCD != screen_code and any subject_EX.EXDOSE > 0) else "N"

# COMPLTFL / DISCONFL / DTHFL from DS (disposition)
COMPLTFL = "Y" if DSTERM contains "Completed" else "N"
DISCONFL = "Y" if COMPLTFL == "N" and not screen failure else "N"
DTHFL    = "Y" if DSTERM contains "Death" else "N"
```

---

## 2. Worked Example

Assume `study_id = "XYZ123"`, `screen_failure_code = "Scrnfail"`.

**DM**
| USUBJID | ARM | ARMCD | AGE | SEX |
|---------|-----|-------|-----|-----|
| XYZ123-001-001 | Placebo | PBO | 45 | F |
| XYZ123-001-002 | Drug A | DRGA | 62 | M |
| XYZ123-002-003 | Scrnfail | Scrnfail | 58 | M |

**EX** (dosing records)
| USUBJID | EXSTDTC | EXENDTC | EXDOSE |
|---------|---------|---------|--------|
| XYZ123-001-001 | 2026-01-05 | 2026-01-05 | 0 (Placebo baseline) |
| XYZ123-001-001 | 2026-01-06 | 2026-02-04 | 10 |
| XYZ123-001-002 | 2026-01-07 | 2026-02-05 | 50 |

**DS**
| USUBJID | DSTERM | DSDECOD |
|---------|--------|---------|
| XYZ123-001-001 | Completed | COMPLETED |
| XYZ123-001-002 | Adverse Event | ADVERSE EVENT |
| XYZ123-002-003 | Screen Failure | SCREEN FAILURE |

**Resulting ADSL**
| USUBJID | TRT01P | TRT01A | TRTSDT | TRTEDT | SAFFL | ITTFL | COMPLTFL | DISCONFL |
|---------|--------|--------|--------|--------|-------|-------|----------|----------|
| XYZ123-001-001 | Placebo | Placebo | 2026-01-06 | 2026-02-04 | Y | Y | Y | N |
| XYZ123-001-002 | Drug A | Drug A | 2026-01-07 | 2026-02-05 | Y | Y | N | Y |
| XYZ123-002-003 | Scrnfail | Scrnfail | null | null | N | N | N | N |

> Note for subject 001: `EXDOSE=0` on 2026-01-05 is excluded from date aggregation, so `TRTSDT` is the first record with `EXDOSE > 0` (2026-01-06).

---

## 3. Edge-Case Handling

| Scenario | Expected Behavior |
|----------|-------------------|
| Screen failure (XYZ123-002-003) | `SAFFL=N`, `ITTFL=N`, no treatment dates; **kept in ADSL** (counted in total subjects) |
| Randomized but never dosed | `SAFFL=N`, `ITTFL=Y`, `TRTSDT/TRTEDT = null` |
| `EX` subject not in `DM` | Flag error; **do NOT** add to ADSL |
| Crossover study | Derive `TRT01P/TRT01A` for period 01; add `TRT02P/TRT02A` as needed |
| Partial `EXSTDTC` | Impute start = 01, end = last day of month |
| `ARM != ACTARM` | Preserve both; document |

---

## 4. Validation Checklist (per `adam-validator`)

After derivation, ADSL must pass:
- **ADSL001/010** — `USUBJID` unique, no duplicates
- **ADSL002** — subject count == `DM`
- **ADSL003** — `SAFFL` per `study_config.population_definitions`
- **ADSL004** — `ITTFL` per randomized criteria
- **ADSL005/006** — `TRT01P`/`TRT01A` populated
- **ADSL007** — `TRTSDT <= TRTEDT` for treated subjects

# AE Overview Table Shell

Below is the complete table shell built to the `tfl-table-generator` + `tfl-formatter` standards (landscape RTF, Courier New 9pt, dynamic treatment columns, integer n / 1-decimal percent, required footnotes).

---

## 1. Table Metadata

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Table ID** | Table 14.3.1 |
| **Title** | Summary of Adverse Events by Treatment Group (Safety Analysis Set) |
| **Population** | Safety (`SAFFL` = 'Y') — note: `SAFFL` typically resides on ADSL; ADAE subjects inherit it |
| **Source dataset** | ADAE |
| **Treatment variable** | `TRT01P` (planned treatment, arm-level columns) |
| **Orientation / Format** | Landscape, Letter, RTF |

---

## 2. Table Shell (Layout)

```
                                   {Arm1}      {Arm2}      ...    Total
                                   (N={n1})    (N={n2})    ...    (N={nt})
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
                                                 n (%)       n (%)     n (%)

Subjects with at least one AE                    __ (__._)   __ (__._) __ (__._)
   Treatment-emergent AEs                        __ (__._)   __ (__._) __ (__._)
   Serious AEs                                   __ (__._)   __ (__._) __ (__._)

AEs by maximum severity †
   Mild                                           __ (__._)   __ (__._) __ (__._)
   Moderate                                       __ (__._)   __ (__._) __ (__._)
   Severe                                         __ (__._)   __ (__._) __ (__._)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

**Column-header rule:** treatment arms and the safety-population N values are dynamically derived from study config (`treatment_arms`) — never hardcoded. `N` is the number of subjects in `SAFFL='Y'`; `n` is subjects with the event; percent = `n / N × 100`, reported to **1 decimal**.

---

## 3. Derivation Logic (from ADAE)

| Row Block | Filter / Logic | Variable |
|-----------|----------------|----------|
| Subjects with at least one AE | distinct `USUBJID` present in ADAE (within `SAFFL='Y'`) | (existence) |
| Treatment-emergent AEs | distinct `USUBJID` where `TRTEMFL = 'Y'` | `TRTEMFL` |
| Serious AEs | distinct `USUBJID` where `AESER = 'Y'` | `AESER` |
| AEs by severity | distinct `USUBJID` per severity category | `ASEV` † |

---

## 4. Structured Spec (machine-readable)

```yaml
table_output:
  table_id: "Table 14.3.1"
  title: "Summary of Adverse Events by Treatment Group (Safety Analysis Set)"
  population: "SAFFL"
  source_dataset: "ADAE"
  treatment_var: "TRT01P"
  format: "rtf"

  columns:
    - { label: "Statistic",            align: "left"   }
    - { label: "{Arm1} (N={n1})",      align: "center" }
    - { label: "{Arm2} (N={n2})",      align: "center" }
    - { label: "Total (N={nt})",       align: "center" }

  rows:
    - block: "Subjects with at least one AE"
      type: "subject-count"
      stat: "n (%)"
      filter: "distinct USUBJID in ADAE"
    - block: "Treatment-emergent AEs"
      type: "subject-count"
      stat: "n (%)"
      filter: "TRTEMFL = 'Y'"
    - block: "Serious AEs"
      type: "subject-count"
      stat: "n (%)"
      filter: "AESER = 'Y'"
    - block: "AEs by maximum severity"
      type: "categorical"
      stat: "n (%)"
      variable: "ASEV"
      categories: ["Mild", "Moderate", "Severe"]
      sort: "fixed-order"

  footnotes:
    - "Protocol: {study_id}"
    - "Population: Safety Analysis Set (SAFFL = 'Y')"
    - "Source: ADAE dataset"
    - "N = number of subjects in the safety analysis set"
    - "n (%) = number and percentage of subjects with the event"
    - "Percentages calculated using N of the treatment group as denominator"
    - "† Subjects counted once at their maximum severity (see assumption note)"
    - "Data cutoff: {data_cut_date}"
```

---

## 5. Assumptions / Dependencies (must confirm before programming)

1. **Severity variable not in scope.** The provided ADAE variables are `TRT01P`, `TRTEMFL`, `AESER` only. Specification #4 ("AEs by severity") requires an additional severity variable — typically **`ASEV`** (MILD/MODERATE/SEVERE) or **`AETOXGR`** (1–5). The shell above assumes `ASEV`. # P21 Validation Review

All four items are **Errors (severity = Error)**, which means each **must be fixed before submission** — none may be justified or deferred without documented sponsor approval. They are ranked below by **regulatory criticality + cascade impact on downstream derivations/analyses**, not by raw record count.

## 1. Severity Ranking

| Rank | Issue | Rule | Records | Why this priority |
|------|-------|------|---------|-------------------|
| **P1** | RFSTDTC missing | SD0007 | 5 subjects | RFSTDTC is the subject reference start date — it anchors **all study-day derivations** (RFSTDY/RFENDY) and exposure-relative time across every findings domain. Missing it silently corrupts time-based analyses for those subjects, even though the count is small. |
| **P2** | Invalid ARMCD = "UNKN" | SD1002 | 1+ subjects | ARMCD is a **required DM key variable** and the foundation of treatment-group analysis (and ADSL). "UNKN" signals an unmapped placeholder rather than a valid CDISC CT arm code, so safety/efficacy by treatment cannot run. |
| **P3** | AEDECOD null | SD0002 | 12 records | AEDECOD (MedDRA preferred term) is required for **standardized AE summaries by preferred term / SOC**. Highest absolute count of broken records. AEs themselves exist, but they cannot be pooled until coded. |
| **P4** | AESTDTC > AEENDTC | SD005x (date logic) | 3 records | Logically impossible dates (start after end). Serious but **isolated to 3 AE records** whose verbatim term and coding are otherwise intact — pure date correction, no downstream schema impact. |

> Note: P4 is the most *obviously wrong* data point (impossible by definition), but ranks last on *submission impact* because it is tightly scoped. If your study's SAP weights AE onset/duration analysis heavily, you may promote it above P3.

## 2. Resolution Steps

### P1 — RFSTDTC missing (5 subjects)
1. Identify the 5 subjects with empty `DM.RFSTDTC` (USUBJID = `{study_id}-{SITEID}-{SUBJID}`).
2. Derive `RFSTDTC` from the subject's **earliest `EX.EXSTDTC`** (first dose/exposure date) — the canonical derivation per the IG.
3. Fallback if no EX record exists: use the randomization/treatment-start disposition record (`DS` where `DSDECOD` = treatment-start term) or first dosing log date; document the fallback rule.
4. Ensure the value conforms to **ISO 8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD`)**; handle partial dates per study rule.
5. Re-run the DM mapper and re-validate with P21 → confirm SD0007 clears.

### P2 — Invalid ARMCD = "UNKN" (SD1002)
1. Pull the full `DM.ARMCD` value list and compare against `study_config.treatment_arms` and the CDISC ARM codelist.
2. Trace "UNKN" back to source (randomization/treatment assignment data) — it is almost certainly a **mapping gap or placeholder**, not a real arm.
3. Map each affected subject to the correct **planned arm code** (≤ 8 chars, alphanumeric only) and ensure `ARM` (full name) is populated consistently.
4. If a subject is genuinely **not randomized / treatment unknown** per protocol, assign the protocol-specified "unassigned" arm code (not the literal string "UNKN") and document the justification.
5. Re-run DM mapper and re-validate.

### P3 — AEDECOD null (12 records) (SD0002)
1. Extract the 12 `AE.AETERM` verbatim terms that have no `AEDECOD`.
2. Route them to **MedDRA coding**; populate `AEDECOD` (Preferred Term).
3. Derive `AEBODSYS` (System Organ Class) from the MedDRA hierarchy for the same records (pre-empt SD0003).
4. Verify the coding uses the MedDRA version matching `study_config.ct_version`.
5. Re-run AE mapper and re-validate.

### P4 — AESTDTC > AEENDTC (3 records)
1. Pull the 3 AE records and trace start/end dates to source (CRF / eDC).
2. Determine the correct dates; enforce **`AESTDTC ≤ AEENDTC`**. Usually the error is a swapped or transposed date.
3. If the end date is genuinely unknown/partial, apply the ISO 8601 partial-date convention and ensure it cannot evaluate as *before* the start; if neither can be resolved, set per study convention (typically leave end blank rather than create a backward interval).
4. Document the corrected values and re-validate.

## 3. Disposition, Verification & Tracking

- **Disposition for all four:** `FIX` — never `JUS`/`DEF` for Errors without sponsor sign-off.
- **Re-validate** after fixes: re-run `p21-validator` to reach **zero errors**, then run `p21-report-reviewer` to record dispositions.
- **Log every resolution** in `ops/p21-sdtm-resolved.yaml` with `disposition: fixed`, per-issue `resolution_notes` (the "why"), affected USUBJIDs, `count`, and `verified: true`.
- **Regression check:** fixing P1/P2 (DM) can ripple into ADSL and study-day fields — confirm no new P21 warnings (e.g., SD0043 "variable not expected") appear after the re-run.

---

# ADSL Derivation from SDTM

Below is a complete, traceable ADSL build following CDISC ADaM IG fundamentals. DM is the backbone (1 record per subject); EX and DS are left-joined. The four requested derivations are implemented with their exact population-flag logic.

## Derivation Logic (one record per subject)

| Variable | Source | Rule |
|----------|--------|------|
| `TRT01P` | DM.ARM | Planned treatment (ARM) |
| `TRT01A` | DM.ACTARM (fallback ARM) | Actual treatment |
| `TRTSDT` | EX (EXDOSE > 0) | `min(EXSTDTC)` among dosed records |
| `TRTEDT` | EX (EXDOSE > 0) | `max(EXENDTC)` among dosed records |
| `SAFFL` | EX + DM | `Y` if ARMCD ≠ screen-failure AND any EXDOSE > 0, else `N` |
| `ITTFL` | DM | `Y` if ARMCD ≠ screen-failure code, else `N` |

## Implementation

```python
"""ADSL derivation: 1 record per subject, foundation for all ADaM analyses."""
import logging
from typing import Optional
import pandas as pd

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _parse_date(s: Optional[str]):
    """Parse a partial ISO date, imputing missing components.

    - '' or None          -> None
    - 'YYYY'              -> YYYY-01-01
    - 'YYYY-MM'           -> YYYY-MM-01
    - 'YYYY-MM-DD'        -> as-is
    """
    if not s or pd.isna(s):
        return None
    s = str(s).strip()
    if len(s) >= 10:
        return pd.to_datetime(s[:10], errors="coerce")
    if len(s) == 7:
        return pd.to_datetime(s + "-01", errors="coerce")
    if len(s) == 4:
        return pd.to_datetime(s + "-01-01", errors="coerce")
    return None


def _is_screen_failure(armcd: str, screen_failure_code: str) -> bool:
    return str(armcd).strip() == screen_failure_code


def derive_population_flags(
    adsl: pd.DataFrame, ex: pd.DataFrame, ds: pd.DataFrame, study_config: dict
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Derive SAFFL and ITTFL per ADaM IG population flag rules."""
    screen_code = study_config.get("screen_failure_code", "Scrnfail")

    # ITTFL: randomized (not a screen failure).
    adsl["ITTFL"] = adsl["ARMCD"].apply(
        lambda c: "Y" if not _is_screen_failure(c, screen_code) else "N"
    )

    # SAFFL: received at least one dose (EXDOSE > 0) and not a screen failure.
    dosed = ex[ex["EXDOSE"].fillna(0) > 0]
    dosed_subjects = set(dosed["USUBJID"].unique())
    adsl["SAFFL"] = adsl.apply(
        lambda r: "Y"
        if (r["USUBJID"] in dosed_subjects and not _is_screen_failure(r["ARMCD"], screen_code))
        else "N",
        axis=1,
    )

    # Disposition flags (downstream convenience, kept minimal here).
    if ds is not None and "DSTERM" in ds.columns:
        completed = set(
            ds.loc[ds["DSTERM"].str.contains("Completed", case=False, na=False), "USUBJID"]
        )
        adsl["COMPLTFL"] = adsl["USUBJID"].apply(lambda u: "Y" if u in completed else "N")

    return adsl


def build_adsl(
    dm: pd.DataFrame, ex: pd.DataFrame, ds: pd.DataFrame, study_config: dict
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build ADSL with 1 record per subject from SDTM DM, EX, DS.

    Args:
        dm: SDTM DM domain (1 record per subject).
        ex: SDTM EX domain (dosing, 1:many).
        ds: SDTM DS domain (disposition).
        study_config: Study config (study_id, screen_failure_code, ...).

    Returns:
        ADSL DataFrame, 1 record per subject.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If DM is not 1 record per subject.
    """
    # --- Backbone: DM must be unique by USUBJID.
    if not dm["USUBJID"].is_unique:
        dupes = dm.loc[dm["USUBJID"].duplicated(), "USUBJID"].tolist()
        raise ValueError(f"DM must have 1 record per subject. Duplicates: {dupes}")

    adsl = dm.copy()

    # --- TRT01P / TRT01A (planned vs. actual treatment).
    adsl["TRT01P"] = adsl["ARM"]
    adsl["TRT01A"] = adsl.get("ACTARM", adsl["ARM"])  # fallback to ARM if ACTARM absent

    # --- TRTSDT / TRTEDT (first/last dose among dosed records).
    dosed = ex[ex["EXDOSE"].fillna(0) > 0].copy() if ex is not None else pd.DataFrame()
    if not dosed.empty:
        dosed["_EXSDT"] = dosed["EXSTDTC"].apply(_parse_date)
        dosed["_EXEDT"] = dosed["EXENDTC"].apply(_parse_date)
        trt_dates = (
            dosed.groupby("USUBJID")
            .agg(TRTSDT=("_EXSDT", "min"), TRTEDT=("_EXEDT", "max"))
            .reset_index()
        )
        adsl = adsl.merge(trt_dates, on="USUBJID", how="left")
    else:
        adsl["TRTSDT"] = None
        adsl["TRTEDT"]

    # --- Population flags.
    adsl = derive_population_flags(adsl, ex, ds, study_config)

    # --- Invariants.
    assert adsl["USUBJID"].is_unique, "ADSL lost 1:1 subject constraint"
    assert len(adsl) == len(dm), "ADSL row count drift from DM"

    logger.info(
        "ADSL built: %d subjects | SAFFL=Y=%d | ITTFL=Y=%d",
        len(adsl), (adsl["SAFFL"] == "Y").sum(), (adsl["ITTFL"] == "Y").sum(),
    )
    return adsl
```

## Quick Verification (dry-run style)

```python
# Subjects with no dose must be SAFFL=N:
assert (adsl.loc[adsl["TRTSDT"].isna(), "SAFFL"] == "N").all()

# Every randomized subject is ITTFL=Y:
assert (adsl.loc[adsl["ITTFL"] == "N", "ARMCD"] == screen_code).all()

# Screen failures carry no treatment dates:
sf = adsl[adsl["ARMCD"] == screen_code]
assert sf[["TRTSDT", "TRTEDT"]].isna().all().all()
```

## Edge-Case Handling (per skill constraints)

| Scenario | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Screen failure (ARMCD = `Scrnfail`) | `SAFFL=N`, `ITTFL=N`, `TRTSDT/TRTEDT=null` |
| Randomized but never dosed | `SAFFL=N`, `ITTFL=Y`, `TRTSDT=null` |
| Partial `EXSTDTC` (YYYY or YYYY-MM) | Impute start=`01`, end=last valid date |
| `ARM ≠ ACTARM` | Preserve both in `TRT01P` / `TRT01A`; do not overwrite |
| EX subject not in DM | Flag error; **never** add to ADSL |
| `EXDOSE ≤ 0` or missing | Excluded from dose-date aggregation |

## Constraints Respected
- **Never:** create >1 record per subject · drop DM subjects · set `SAFFL=Y` without EX records · hardcode arms.
- **Always:** DM as backbone · left-join EX/DS · validate 1:1 subject constraint · resolve screen-failure code from `study_config`.

```

2. Implemented the 4 requested derivations: SAFFL, ITTFL, TRT01P/TRT01A, TRTSDT/TRTEDT

📊 Current Status
• Reference implementation only — no files written (no --input-dir/output provided)
• Invariants asserted: 1:1 USUBJID, row count == DM, SAFFL/ITTFL consistency

💡 Next Steps
1. Provide --input-dir / --output paths to materialize adsl.xpt via adam-adsl-builder
2. Add AGEGR1 (cutoff from study_config) and DTHFL/COMPLTFL if needed downstream
3. Run /adam-validator + /adam-traceability-checker before consuming in ADAE/ADTTE/ADEFF
```

# SAP Extraction — NCT048 Phase 3 Trial

## 1. Primary Endpoint (with timepoint)

| Element | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Parameter** | Change from Baseline in HbA1c (%) |
| **Timepoint** | Week 24 |
| **Structure** | BDS continuous (AVAL = HbA1c at Week 24; BASE = HbA1c at baseline; CHG = AVAL − BASE) |
| **Implied ADaM target** | `PARAMCD` = HBA1C (or CFBLHBA1C), `AVISIT` = Week 24, `ABLFL` = baseline record |

> **Derivation note:** This is a CHG (change from baseline) endpoint → BASE must be derived from the `ABLFL='Y'` record, and `PCHG = (CHG/BASE)*100` is recommended for completeness.

---

## 2. Secondary Endpoints

| # | Endpoint | Type | Implied PARAMCD / Structure |
|---|----------|------|------------------------------|
| 1 | **HbA1c < 7.0% at Week 24** | Responder (binary) | OCCDS-style; `AVALC` = "Y"/"N"; threshold **7.0% is hardcoded in SAP, must not be hardcoded in code** — read from config |
| 2 | **Body weight change** | Continuous change from baseline | BDS; CHG = weight at timepoint − baseline weight |

> **Responder rule (Sec 1):** A subject is a responder (`AVALC='Y'`) if Week 24 HbA1c < 7.0%. The 7.0% threshold is the SAP-defined responder criterion — store in `sap-parsed.yaml`, never inline.

---

## 3. Population Definitions (exact criteria)

| Population | Flag | Exact Criteria |
|------------|------|----------------|
| **ITT (Intent-to-Treat)** | `ITTFL` | Randomized **AND** dosed (received any study drug) |
| **Safety** | `SAFFL` | Received **any dose** of study drug (`EXDOSE > 0`) |
| **Per-Protocol (PP)** | `PPROTFL` | No protocol deviations (ITT + no major deviations) |

### Derived flag logic (from study-config defaults)

```python
# SAFFL — any dose received
SAFFL = "Y" if DM.ARMCD != screen_failure_code and any(EX.EXDOSE > 0) else "N"

# ITTFL — randomized + dosed
# NOTE: This SAP defines ITT as "randomized AND dose",
# which is STRICTER than the default (default ITT = randomized only).
ITTFL = "Y" if (ARMCD != screen_failure_code) and (any EXDOSE > 0) else "N"

# PPROTFL — ITT + completed + no major deviations
PPROTFL = "Y" if ITTFL == "Y" and COMPLTFL == "Y" and no_major_deviations else "N"
```

> ⚠️ **Important SAP deviation to document:** The default `ITTFL` derivation treats **randomization alone** as sufficient for ITT. **This SAP adds a dosing requirement** ("randomized + dose"). This discrepancy must be:
> 1. Documented in the **ADRG** as a study-specific override,
> 2. Driven by `sap-parsed.yaml`, not by the builder default.

---

## 4. Statistical Method

| Element | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Primary method** | **MMRM** (Mixed Model for Repeated Measures) |
| **Applies to** | Primary endpoint (Change from Baseline HbA1c at Week 24) |
| **Typical model** | Fixed effects: treatment, visit, treatment×visit interaction, baseline HbA1c as covariate; unstructured covariance; ITT population |

> MMRM implies the analysis uses **all post-baseline longitudinal data** (not just Week 24), so the ADaM dataset must retain the full visit sequence with proper `AVISIT`/`PARAMCD` records, not collapse to a single Week-24 row.

---

## ⚠️ Flags for ADEFF Builder & ADRG

1. **Hardcoded threshold risk** — The "7.0%" responder criterion and "Week 24" timepoint must be read from `sap-parsed.yaml`, never inline.
2. **ITT definition conflict** — SAP's ITT (randomized + dose) differs from the ADaM default (randomized only). Override via config + document in ADRG.
3. **Responder endpoint** — HbA1c < 7.0% → OCCDS structure with `AVALC`; both `AVAL` and `AVALC` should be consistent where possible.
4. **MMRM requirement** — Preserve longitudinal structure; do not pre-collapse visits in ADEFF.

---

📋 **Operation Review**
1. Extracted 4 data elements (primary endpoint, secondaries, populations, method) from SAP excerpt
2. Cross-referenced against ADaM derivation conventions (BDS/OCCDS, ABLFL, responder flags)

📊 **Current Status**
• Extraction complete; 2 SAP-vs-default conflicts flagged (ITT definition, hardcoded thresholds)
